Disappointing and I would not recommend

In January, I purchased a car from Partridge Motor Cars, within two days I was emailed asking if I would give a Google 5 stars review, I decided not to do this as I wanted to wait to see if there were any issues with the car, before I left a review. Within one week there was a significant problem with water in a rear footwell, then two days later it wouldn't start. I called a breakdown service, after inspecting the car, the mechanic found significant issues with the car - including several water leaks, water in the battery tray, the fuel pump wasn't working properly and the ignition was sticking. It was returned to Partridge Motor Cars ten days after purchasing it. After approximately two/three weeks I was given a courtesy car. I frequently had to call for updates about my car, I received very few 'promised' return callbacks, people became 'unavailable' when I called for updates, overall it was exceptionally poor customer service. The car was returned to me almost six weeks later, and within 10 hours the car was not starting, I called a breakdown service and it appeared that there was an issue with the' fixed /replaced' fuel pump and there was water in the same rear footwell, as had been 'repaired' during the previous almost six weeks that Partridge Motor Cars had had my car. I returned the car requesting a full refund, which took over a week to be processed, I have incurred 'significant costs', approximately £300, due to purchasing a car that appears to have been 'not fit for purpose'. I was offered a courtesy car and a six-month warranty, I refused this, as I had no trust in the vehicle or the company at this point. As a parting gift from Partridge Motor Cars, after two months, they had still not transferred ownership of the vehicle to me, despite me emailing the Proprietor, to enquire whether this had happened, so if I hadn't made further enquiries with the DVLA, I would not have received the refund for the Vehicle Tax, Partridge Motor Cars would have received it! I would not recommend Partridge Motors to someone that I didn't like, I experienced consistently poor service, a lack of communication, a lack of accountability and have lost out financially through no fault of my own.

I’m very disappointed with the “Own a Pony Day” experience at Polegate Equestrian Centre, especially considering the £55 cost.
The day did not reflect what most people would reasonably expect from an “own a pony” experience. There was no mucking out, no grooming, and no opportunity to tack up the pony. The children also didn’t get any real time to bond with or care for the horses, such as petting or handling them properly.
The hack itself was very short and grouped children of mixed ability together. This made the experience unfair, particularly for more experienced riders who didn’t get the level of riding they would expect.
Lunch was also very disappointing. We were told lunch would be provided, but it consisted of just four chicken nuggets and a small packet of chips, which is not adequate for a full-day activity.
Additionally, the instructor was not particularly helpful or fair, which added to the overall negative experience.

For £55, an “Own a Pony Day” should include:
- Hands-on stable care (such as mucking out)
- Grooming and preparing the pony
- Learning and participating in tacking up
- Meaningful time spent interacting and bonding with the pony
- A well-structured and appropriately grouped riding session based on ability
- A proper, sufficient lunch
- Supportive and attentive instruction

Overall, this experience did not deliver on its promise, and I would not recommend it based on our visit.

Like many others, I honestly do not know where to begin. However, in the interests of fairness, I will start with the positives.

My initial contact was with Leanne, who was efficient, professional, and informative throughout the sales process. Once the order was placed, communication moved over to Chantal and unfortunately, that is where the problems really started.

The packing team arrived on 6th December exactly on time, were polite, professional, and packed everything well. Prior to their arrival, I had already carefully wrapped many items myself in bubble wrap.

Now for the nightmare that followed.

We booked a shared container shipment and fully understood there could be some waiting time for consolidation with another customer. However, we ultimately waited over two months before the container even set sail, which in my opinion was completely unreasonable. The vessel finally departed on 11th February.

Below is a factual timeline of the communication and delays from emails:

• 6th Dec — Shipment collected from Chester
• 5th Jan — I emailed Chantal for an update. She advised loading would likely occur during January with approximately 8 weeks transit time
• 9th Jan — ReloUK sent a generic update email with no loading dates, specifically asking customers not to reply
• 16th Jan — Another generic email was sent asking customers not to reply. Due to urgency, I replied anyway and was advised loading would take place week commencing 26th January
• 26th Jan — I emailed with a Dubai address update and was advised the container had been loaded
• 2nd Feb — I chased again and was told there were further delays
• 3rd Feb — I expressed frustration and explained the urgency of the situation
• 7th Feb — Sally requested escalation details after nearly two months without departure
• 9th Feb — Chantal provided the complaints procedure
• 11th Feb — Tammy finally provided vessel details confirming the shipment had sailed

We then received communication from the UAE shipping company advising the vessel would arrive in early March. Unfortunately, war then broke out in the Middle East and the vessel was diverted to Oman.

Of course, no company can foresee a regional conflict. However, because of the enormous delays before the shipment had even left the UK, we were then hit with over £2,000 in additional war surcharges, detention fees, and customs-related costs before the container could be released.

At this point, I contacted Chantal requesting the matter be escalated internally, as we felt these additional costs were completely unacceptable given the delays already experienced. We were then passed to Paul, the Managing Director.

Sadly, the response from Paul was extremely disappointing. Rather than showing empathy or offering any form of goodwill gesture, his emails felt defensive, dismissive, sarcastic and at times unnecessarily confrontational. We were even accused of being aggressive towards staff, despite the considerable stress and frustration caused by the situation.

Throughout the entire process, we never once felt reassured or supported. Every issue was met with excuses rather than solutions. Whilst the war itself was clearly outside anyone’s control, the lengthy delay before departure absolutely was not.

We eventually received our shipment two weeks ago, but the overall experience was one of the most stressful service experiences we have dealt with. I can positively say only a few wine glasses and a ceramic bowl were broken during the containers epic journey.

In hindsight, I genuinely wish I had paid more and used a larger, more established relocation company such as Crown Relocations. Although their initial quote was higher, I suspect the overall process would have been significantly smoother, quicker, and potentially cheaper once all additional charges were taken into account.

Based on our experience, I personally would not recommend ReloUK.

I DO NOT recommend going with ReloUK for any international move.
You may be enticed by the lower quote when compared to other international moving companies, but there is a reason for this, and that's low quality of the service.

Extremely disappointing experience with One Day Test during an already stressful IVF process.

Before purchasing their IVF Viral Screen, I specifically contacted customer services to confirm the testing was UKAS accredited because this was a requirement for our IVF clinic. Based on the assurances given, we proceeded with the testing.

The service is advertised as containing the IVF virology blood tests “usually requested by the clinics”, however our IVF clinic later rejected the results because the virology testing did not meet the required UKAS accreditation standards for IVF treatment.

What made this even more frustrating was the lack of transparency. The test reports were headed with One Day Test and Sussex Pathology branding, with no clear indication that the virology testing had actually been outsourced to another laboratory. It then took weeks of emails and a formal complaint before this was finally explained to us.

As a result, we had to urgently pay £552 to repeat the blood tests elsewhere in order to avoid delays to our IVF treatment, on top of the £347 already spent with One Day Test.

Despite this, One Day Test refused to provide a refund or acknowledge that the tests were not suitable for our IVF clinic’s requirements, even though we had specifically checked UKAS accreditation with them before purchasing.

IVF is stressful enough without unnecessary confusion, delays, and additional costs. I strongly feel there should be much clearer information provided to patients about outsourced testing and accreditation scope before purchase.

I am deeply disappointed in how Wise Payments Ltd handled a recent fraud incident that left me without any savings and only £29 in my account, causing extreme financial and emotional distress. On August 21st, 2024, I was scammed by a criminal impersonating a member of Wise’s fraud team, withdrawing nearly £2,000 from my account. Despite contacting Wise immediately, their response was slow and inadequate. They failed to contact Trading 212 (where my funds were transferred) promptly, leaving me to handle the situation with minimal support. Wise assured me they would attempt to recover the money, but this process could take up to 50 days and is not guaranteed.

Wise has been well aware that their customers are being targeted by a criminal organisation impersonating their fraud team, yet they refuse to take accountability or implement sufficient changes to their safeguarding measures. This has led to repeated incidents of fraud, with little action taken to prevent it from happening over and over again. I know of half a dozen people in the last few months who have fallen victim to this particular scam, and God only knows how many others feel too ashamed to come forward. Furthermore, they are notorious for closing customers’ accounts without explanation, as documented by countless members in the Wise (TransferWise) Scam Victims Facebook group, which has over 19,000 members.

What’s worse, when you report fraudulent activity, Wise will gaslight you into thinking the incident is your fault, often offering only 50% ‘compensation’ for your stolen funds, despite their own system’s failure to protect customers. I received no warning notifications and was not adequately informed about the scam risks despite their knowledge of similar incidents occurring. Their fraud detection measures are inadequate, and they failed to notify me directly through text or phone call when my account was compromised.

Wise’s lack of accountability is alarming. With the new APP Fraud law set to take effect in October, Wise and other financial institutions will be held to higher standards for customer protection. I sincerely hope this forces them to improve their fraud prevention and customer support.

In addition, I have been waiting for 101 days for a response to my SAR (Subject Access Request), which has been completely ignored. All my attempts to communicate since submitting my formal complaint have gone unanswered. I’ve asked important questions, including whether Wise has reported the scam to the relevant authorities, what measures have been implemented since, and how they are addressing the ongoing fraud issues. Yet, no response has been provided.

Given my experience and the ongoing issues documented by other victims, I absolutely cannot recommend Wise. They fail to take responsibility for their customers’ protection, and their response to fraud is insufficient, both in prevention and in resolving the damage caused. Wise must make DRASTIC improvements if they are to regain the trust of their customers.

I initially instructed Bespoke Law Services to assist with the sale of my leasehold property. As the matter progressed it became apparent that a Deed of Variation to the ground rent provisions of my lease would be required before a sale could proceed, and the firm took on this additional matter.

Unfortunately the experience fell well below the standard I expected from a regulated firm.

Throughout the matter I experienced persistent delays in responses, with one email going unanswered for over 34 days. On multiple occasions I had to chase repeatedly to receive any update. When responses were received they were often a single line and failed to address the substance of my questions.

A specific instruction I gave in writing was ignored for over 34 days with no acknowledgement or explanation at the time. When I raised a formal complaint, my file was subsequently closed without my agreement while the complaint remained unresolved.

I have submitted a Subject Access Request under UK GDPR which has not been responded to within the statutory 30-day deadline, and I am currently exploring further escalation options available to me.

I would caution anyone considering using this firm for conveyancing matters to carefully consider the level of service they may receive.

Update — 28 April 2026

Following the closure of my file, I submitted a Subject Access Request under UK GDPR requesting all personal data held by the firm, including recorded telephone calls. The firm failed to respond within the statutory 30-day deadline, which I have reported to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO). When a response was eventually provided, it was incomplete — omitting the majority of substantive correspondence, all emails sent to third parties on my behalf, and all telephone recordings despite the firm's own policy stating all calls are recorded. I have formally challenged the adequacy of the response and updated my ICO report accordingly. I have also submitted formal complaints to the Legal Ombudsman and the Council of Licensed Conveyancers. I would strongly advise anyone considering using this firm to carefully research their recent reviews and regulatory record before instructing them.

Update — 29 April 2026

The firm responded to this review within 19 hours stating they would "look into my case and get back to me directly." I would note that this response time still stands in stark contrast to the 34+ days it took to respond to a formal email instruction during the course of my matter. I have now submitted formal complaints to the Legal Ombudsman and the Council of Licensed Conveyancers, reported a breach of UK GDPR to the Information Commissioner's Office, and am pursuing an incomplete Subject Access Request response. The firm has been unable to confirm whether telephone recordings of our calls exist, despite their own email footer stating all calls are recorded for monitoring and training purposes. I maintain my original review in full.

Update — 13 May 2026

The firm has now failed to meet both the statutory 30-day GDPR deadline (26 April 2026) and a further deadline I set of 12 May 2026 for a complete Subject Access Request response. The SAR remains incomplete — telephone recordings have not been provided despite the firm's own communications stating all calls are recorded, emails sent to third parties on my behalf have been withheld, and internal file notes have not been disclosed. I recently had a very different experience while sending goods to Bangladesh through E-One Cargo. I later discovered that the company's management had changed. The previous owner was excellent—he delivered goods very quickly and always kept his promises. Unfortunately, this time around, my experience was quite different, which prompted me to share my feedback.

I called last month on April 13, 2026, and my home delivery items were picked up from my house on April 14, 2026. When I asked about the timeline, the representative informed me that the goods would be dispatched on Friday, April 17. He told me it would take one week for the items to arrive in Bangladesh.However, after waiting two weeks, the goods still had not reached their destination. Due to an emergency, I called them again to check on the status, and I was told the delay was due to customs issues. At that time, he assured me the problem would hopefully be resolved by May 12, 2026. Since then, they have completely stopped answering my calls.

I paid the full amount for my delivery and packaging charges immediately. However, I have not received the service I paid for, and he is no longer answering my phone calls. I have spoken with other cargo companies, and I understand that while their shipments are reaching Bangladesh without issue, E-One Cargo is facing customs problems. Furthermore, he has not provided clear information regarding the destination or status of my goods. It appears my items were either sent via a cheaper, delayed method to cut costs, or they were not dispatched on time.It dawned on me slowly, and then all at once.I was the victim of a clever scam.l recently realized that my shipment might be a victim of fraud. Several other customers used different cargo services, and their shipments arrived in just one week.How is it possible that only your cargo company is experiencing customs issues? If there were a legitimate customs delay, it would affect everyone's cargo, not just mine.

Based on my past good experiences, I recently sent goods to Bangladesh through E One Cargo. I was shocked to find out that the ownership had changed, and I ended up being scammed. It’s really unfair how one or two bad dishonest individuals cause people to unfairly judge an entire community.

Today, May 14, 2026, after waiting a long month, I finally received my shipment. It was such a bitter experience that I had to share what happened so no one else falls victim to this kind of fraud. Hopefully, reading about my ordeal will help save others from being scammed.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm unhappy with the professional standards and conduct of Fusion Consulting group.In or around June 2025, my company engaged Fusion Consultancy for tax planning and advisory services at a cost of approx £21,000. The service was presented to me as a comprehensive and bespoke tax strategy for both company and personal matters.

The service sold to me was materially misrepresented and fell significantly below the professional standards I would expect from an ATT-affiliated practice.

Fusion have used misleading representations regarding scope of services.
The proposal documentation referred to the “Delivery of Master Tax Strategy”, which reasonably implies a complete planning and delivery service. At no stage was it made sufficiently clear that the £21,000 fee related primarily to a written report only, and that substantial additional implementation fees would later be demanded.

In fact, after receiving the report, I was informed that implementation of the recommendations would require a further payment of approximately £21,000. Bringing the total cost to £42,000

Had this been made transparently clear from the outset, I would never have agreed to proceed as this would not be financially justified for our business.

In actual fact. I had originally declined Fusions services, stating that I thought the cost was not proportionate to the saving I would make. This then lead to Mitch Young (director of Fusion) making misleading assurances regarding value and financial benefit
He said:
“I can certainly assure you that the savings you would make short and long term would significantly outweigh the costs.” (e mail dated 12th June 8.37am)

At no point within these discussions was it properly clarified that substantial additional implementation fees would be required before any alleged savings could realistically be achieved. Mitch Young painted a picture that with £21k we would see savings that far outweighed this cost. He never mentioned that an additional £21k would be needed, bringing the total to £42k. I believe this created a misleading impression that the quoted fee covered the overall planning and delivery process.

Mitch went one step further to get us past the line. He made assurances that if my company did not make savings that outweighed the cost, he would refund us. This was what offered me the assurance I needed.

Fusion produced a report for us for tax planning. I was shocked when they requested another £21k to implement ANY of the steps in the report. I had up until this point been under the impression we were paying for an end to end service. My company cannot pay £42k for tax implementation. this means the £21k we paid was literally for only a report, that will not deliver any level of saving unless I pay further to implement anything.

The report itself is of my opinion, a non-bespoke product. This is because the report contained another individual’s name and company details within the document. This strongly indicated that the report had been adapted from pre-existing material rather than prepared specifically for my circumstances.

I experienced what I considered inappropriate professional conduct from the Director, who attempted to contact me via personal TikTok direct messages despite me being a paying client. When the point was raised, he swiftly deleted this account and his complaints handler has outright denied any communication of a personal nature via Tik Tok.

When I had requested a partial refund for the above breaches in professional standards and conduct. Fusion have refused, going as far as threatening me for leaving a review of my experience. They have also made a statement saying that consumer rights don't apply as it was my company that engaged in their service. What they fail to understand is that as a member of the ATT they are obligated and bound by certain rules, one of which is that they must not engage in misleading or deceptive conduct.

one_star_reviews.text:
Have you ever had a meal so catastrophically bad it looped back around to entertaining? Welcome to the Crown and Anchor, less a dining experience and more a group therapy session. We were returning after a few years. Six of us, five adults and one child who, frankly, has now been traumatised. The place has become tired, a little grubby, and was completely silent. No music.  Just silence. The kind of oppressive quiet where you can hear other diners softly questioning their life choices. Imagine a library, but the books are all menus and everything is disappointing.

We had a 12:30 reservation, which the restaurant treated as more of a loose suggestion. Tables were hastily thrown together, cutlery-free, condiment-free, and atmosphere-free. A trifecta of nothing.

Drinks arrived quickly though, so full marks there.

Then came the food. I genuinely wish I’d photographed it for posterity, or as evidence. The sausage and mash was served with a gravy so thick and gelatinous it had transcended the concept of gravy entirely and become something closer to jam. Brown, wobbly, inexplicable jam. The sausages were grey. Not “slightly pale” grey. Grey grey. The fish and chips were completely flavourless — the fish somehow managing to be both wet and tough simultaneously, which I didn’t think was physically possible. The peas were cold and undercooked, which takes real commitment.

The pepperoni pizza arrived with exactly eight lonely pieces of pepperoni adrift in a sea of congealed, oily cheese. Eight. We counted. The Caesar salad had so much tasteless dressing, it was less a salad and more a soup.

The banana bloom and chips were fine. Greasy, but fine.  The gammon was good. Whoever made it clearly wandered in from a different, better restaurant. My father-in-law was happy, blissfully unaware of the carnage around him.

The waitresses were lovely, warm, professional, and visibly innocent of any involvement in the cooking. When I paid the £130 bill at the bar and explained that most of the meal had been, to put it diplomatically, a disaster, the manager informed me her hands were tied. Why? Because my wife had told the waitress everything was fine. Never mind that this check happened approximately two minutes after the food landed on the table, barely enough time to identify what you were looking at, let alone form an opinion. Apparently that two-minute window is legally binding.

So there you have it. The Crown and Anchor: silent as a crypt, grey sausages, jam gravy, and a complaints policy that would impress a used car dealer. Highly recommend if you enjoy eating in a library that’s also on fire.

Due to the aggregate being larger, when I done the pour I had a hard time leveling it correctly and now I have  to spend extra time and money to grind the concrete down. Also I had to pay for extra material (1 cubic meter) as it was more material going in due to it being hard to maneuver and level. Needles to say, I won't be using them again!
But I am concerned about the strength of my slab due to the 110mm thickness with 20mm aggregate.

Following the response from the owner, I have to reiterate the fact that I did complain to IMix at the time, email and phones but they simply didn't admit any wrong doing. They eventually provided cube tests which I didn't witnessed being done when the slab was poured. If the cubes were poured with my material, they would have seen the larger aggregates. Its just the whole behaviour being very shady and not trustworthy. I am downgrading to 1 star because of this.

Very disappointed and honestly quite upset by the way Battersea handled my dog’s ongoing rehabilitation treatment.
My dog has been receiving hydrotherapy, laser and physiotherapy treatment through Battersea for over 3 years, with regular appointments required as part of a long term rehabilitation plan. During that time, I spent a significant amount of money with the service and always followed their strict cancellation policy, including paying full cancellation charges without dispute whenever I missed an appointment.

Unfortunately, the same level of fairness and accountability was never shown in return.
Recently there were repeated last minute physiotherapy cancellations, including one cancelled by email at 7:41pm the evening before the appointment, giving 12 hours notice. This email could very easily have been missed, and for something this important, a simple phone call would have been the respectful and responsible thing to do. For a dog requiring ongoing pain management and rehabilitation, this level of disruption is incredibly stressful. At no stage was any alternative support, such as offering hydrotherapy treatment in place of physiotherapy ever suggested.

I completely understand that pregnancy related illness and unforeseen circumstances happen, and I genuinely wish Megan and her baby all the best. However, cancelling 2 out of the last 3 physiotherapy appointments made it almost impossible to maintain continuity of care for my dog.

What shocked me most was the complete lack of compassion or accountability from management afterwards. Battersea has an extremely strict cancellation policy for customers, charging 100% of the appointment cost with no exceptions, yet when their own service repeatedly failed to deliver appointments, there was absolutely no balance, flexibility or goodwill shown in return.

I requested what I believed was a very modest and reasonable goodwill gesture of one hydrotherapy session, or the value of £70, after years of loyalty and support. Instead, I was met with cold corporate style responses repeating policies and stating, “we are a charity,” while at the same time charging for services like any other business. The hydrotherapy and physiotherapy department operates as a business within a charity, yet there appeared to be none of the compassion or understanding you would expect from an organisation that publicly promotes putting dogs first.

I also requested communication directly from someone within the management team, and that request was ignored entirely. To this day, nobody from management has contacted me personally.

What makes this even worse is that there appears to be no proper backup system when appointments are cancelled. Clients are simply pushed to the back of the queue and expected to work around already very limited availability. That is simply not acceptable for animals relying on ongoing rehabilitation treatment.

After years of support, I expected a far more balanced, compassionate and understanding approach. Instead, the experience left me feeling like I was dealing with a vicious corporation hiding behind charity branding, where policies and revenue mattered more than the wellbeing and continuity of care for the dogs relying on the service.

I am now left with the stress of trying to find an entirely new rehabilitation team for my dog while she remains in pain and without the continuity of treatment she needs. Sadly, I no longer trust the Battersea team.

I would strongly advise anyone considering using 1 Answer Insurance to just not.

I made it clear to the advisor before the policy even started that I did not need cover until a week later, as I did not yet have the vehicle. Despite this, the policy was still initiated early, which resulted in me being insured on a car I did not even own at the time.

I cancelled within the 14-day cooling-off period, and I have been told I will be charged for a full week of cover that I explicitly said I did not need.

To add to this, I have now had a further £87.34 taken from my account without my permission, on top of the £210.15 I had already paid as a deposit. I have received no refund to date, and no clear explanation of the additional deduction.

End result:

Paying for insurance I did not need
Additional charge of £87.34 taken without consent
£210.15 already paid with no refund issued
A cancellation process that has effectively charged me over 20% of the overall cover cost for 7 days' insurance on a vehicle they know I didn't own at the time of cover and a policy which was cancelled within the 14 day cooling off period.

FYI, if anyone is unhappy with how their complaint is handled by No Answer Insurance, they can escalate it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. This is a free process for consumers. The business is charged a case fee by the Ombudsman per complaint ☺️ which is typically several hundred pounds (up to £650) once the initial free allowance of 3 cases is exceeded within a financial year, regardless of the outcome.

I would strongly advise anyone considering using 1 Answer Insurance to just not do it.

I made it clear to the advisor before the policy even started that I did not need coverage until a week later than the initial proposed start date, as I didn’t yet have the vehicle. Despite this, the policy was still started early, leaving me insured on a car I didn’t even own.

I am still within the 14-day cooling-off period, yet the policy has not been cancelled after multiple requests that it should be cancelled, and I’m being told I’ll be charged for the full week of cover I explicitly said I did not need. To make matters worse, the delays on their side mean I’m now being charged for additional days of cover after multiple requests to cancel.

I’ve also been told that the insurer has issued a cancellation amount that is somehow higher than the total policy cost, which even they believe is incorrect. So I’m now stuck waiting while they “figure it out,” with no clarity on what I’ll actually be charged.

End result:
- Paying for insurance I didn’t need
- Delays increasing the cost
- No clear answers
- A process that feels completely out of my control

Overall, this has been a frustrating and unnecessarily complicated experience. I would avoid this company at all costs.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you are looking for a PhD programme that prioritizes "administrative performance art" over basic communication, look no further than the RCA. It has truly earned its "World No.1" ranking—specifically in the category of total bureaucratic dysfunction.

I applied for the PhD with one of their full funding in Round 1 (submitted in Dec). According to their published "key dates", outcomes for Round 1 should have been notified by “late Feb”. Apparently, RCA's concept of timeline is much like its approach to applicant communication: abstract, non-linear, and unrivalled silence.

After weeks of follow-up emails disappearing into a black hole, I eventually received a "soft" rejection via the scholarship team in April—nearly two months late, and only because I persistently chased for an answer through their three different teams:

1. Admissions team: First inquiry sent in late Feb → auto-reply promising a response "within three working days" (now sounding more like a British punchline) → no response for two weeks → first follow-up → another week of silence → second follow-up → silence ever since.

2. Scholarship team: Inquiry sent in early March → after three weeks of silence, a confused reply: "I believe the outcomes were released earlier and you should have received a notification from the School to which you were applying" → I confirmed there had been no notification or portal update → "we will look into what has gone wrong" → another LOVELY THREE WEEKS later, they finally confirmed that "the studentship panel for 2026 has met and confirmed that unfortunately, you have been unsuccessful."

*What exactly do they mean by "has met", after previously claiming the outcomes had already been released? The communication became even more evasive when they ignored my question about whether funding interviews had taken place or if invitations had already been issued—the selection process for this funding never clearly stated on their website; the funding quotas (home vs. international) was also never disclosed.

3. School team: no response at all. Their commitment to the "administrative performance" is impressive: my application portal STILL reads "Application Under Review". A rather polished piece of digital fiction.

Meanwhile, throughout this entire period of silence, I have been bombarded by annoying promotional emails including a celebration of RCA's "No.1 QS ranking 2026". So communication is clearly not the issue—it is simply reserved for marketing. It is difficult not to connect this with the volume of concerns raised by current and former master's students, many of whom question whether the highest tuition fees reflect genuine educational quality or something closer to a highly polished business "fraud" lacking decent academic and administrative support.

It seems the "RCA Experience" begins with being ignored and somehow "played" by an admissions system that treats applicant emails like unsolicited spam. For prospective applicants: if you value transparency, basic professional courtesy, or having your emails acknowledged, you may want to look elsewhere for your "No.1" experience.

I am also aware of other applicants in the same round who are still receiving no communication at all. This is not what one expects from a reputable institution—it's closer to a high-priced administrative vanishing act. Delays can happen; complete absence and equivocation of communication should not—especially from an institution that positions itself at the very top.

one_star_reviews.text:
We had a very disappointing experience renting through Orlando Reid, particularly at the end of the tenancy. We only lived in the flat for seven months after receiving a no‑fault eviction four months in, yet were met with an unreasonable and ultimately unsuccessful attempt to retain a large portion of our deposit.

End of tenancy and deposit dispute:
Despite the condition the property was in when we moved in, and the fact we fully cooperated with sale viewings during our final months, the letting agent attempted to deduct £650 from our deposit.

This included £80 for a tiny bathroom chip and £160 for a small kitchen chip, as well as alleged cleaning costs. The chips were minor, and we had photos showing they were present at check‑in (though poorly documented in the inventory). The claim that the flat was left unclean was frustrating given the standard it was handed to us in.

We had no option but to go through the tenancy deposit scheme dispute process, which resulted in the agent being awarded only £85 of the £650 claimed.
Photos attached show the size of the chips and the issues referenced below.

Maintenance and safety issues:
A number of problems were raised early and either took too long to resolve or were never dealt with:

- A bathroom radiator marked “unsafe” at inventory was never fixed.
- A leak from the flat above took a long time to sort and left a large ceiling stain for months before eventually being painted over, despite repeated chasing.
- Both the bathroom and kitchen extractor fans broke within weeks of moving in. The bathroom is internal with no other ventilation. We reported this immediately, but after months of emails were told repairs would not take place for another two months. After we received our no‑fault eviction, the repairs were simply cancelled, despite us still living in the property for several more months. We had to request a dehumidifier ourselves.
- During a building key‑fob change, we were left without access to the building for six days. We repeatedly tried to escalate this as urgent, but were largely left to chase building management ourselves.

Condition at move‑in:
Despite being a modern property, the flat was not clean when we moved in. It was not professionally cleaned and fell short even of a domestic standard. There were heavy stains on furniture and carpets, and mould already present in the kitchen and bathroom. We ended up cleaning the property ourselves at the start of the tenancy.

Overall:
Overall, the experience felt like Orlando Reid was far quicker to pursue money from tenants than to address safety, maintenance, or fair treatment. Based on our experience, I would not recommend renting through this agency.

After my experience with DCK Solicitors, I believe people should know exactly what they might face before signing contracts or paying large legal fees.

I paid around £2,500 to DCK Solicitors to assist with my immigration matter, trusting them with a case that directly affected my future and my family’s life in the UK.

Unfortunately, my application was later rejected as invalid. Throughout the process, there was confusion regarding key issues relating to documents and the handling of the application. Following later discussions with the firm, concerns surrounding mistakes in the application process were acknowledged. As a client, I expected important issues to be identified and addressed clearly from the outset. Instead, I found myself trying to understand major aspects of my own case after the fact.

What concerned me most was what happened next. After already paying approximately £2,500, I contacted the firm to discuss the situation and next steps. I was then informed that a further payment of approximately £1,000 would be needed to continue and effectively redo work on the case. After investing significant money, trust and time, this left me feeling frustrated and questioning the level of care and responsibility taken with my matter.

Eventually I lost confidence in allowing the firm to continue handling my case and decided to proceed independently.

My advice to anyone considering DCK Solicitors: ask detailed questions, understand possible additional costs, and ensure everything is clearly confirmed in writing before signing anything. Immigration matters affect families and futures, and clients deserve clarity and confidence throughout the process.

This review reflects my personal experience.

Absolutely terrible behaviour and rubbish customer service. Avoid!

I spent just over £5000 On a second hand car from this business.
On the drive home after purchasing the car, the engine management light came on. I reported immediately. I was then asked to drive the vehicle back despite not knowing what fault the car had. I had to limp the car an hour from home back to the garage. The issue was eventually identified as a faulty spark plug.

Less than a week later, the only key supplied with the vehicle failed completely, not a battery issue but an electronic degrading. I had to arrange repair at my own expense because the dealership repeatedly delayed engaging with the issue while claiming they were “investigating”.

Only days later, the engine management light returned again. All of this happened within the first three weeks of ownership.

What followed was weeks of exhausting and unnecessary correspondence. I was subjected to what felt like relentless badgering, with close to 100 contacts back and forth trying to argue over responsibility and deductions instead of simply resolving the matter properly. Most responses appeared to be copied-and-pasted ChatGPT style replies with little genuine engagement with the actual issues being raised, which became incredibly frustrating and draining to deal with.
It became a little joke to put my message that I had sent to LMS into ChatGPT and my husband and I reading out the response and giggling that we received a word for word chatGPT response to my messages.

I became exhausted from having to repeatedly cite the Consumer Rights Act simply to explain basic consumer protections that should already have been understood and respected by a motor dealership. It felt as though the law was being treated as optional guidance, with attempts being made to pick and choose which parts were convenient to follow. I repeatedly had to explain that consumers are legally protected when rejecting a faulty vehicle and that the responsibility for collection rests with the dealership once a valid rejection has been made.

I then spent over a week arguing for the vehicle to be collected while continuing to be told the matter was “being investigated”, despite the car sitting on my driveway the entire time. I was forced to obtain an AA inspection report at my own expense simply to move matters forward.

When the vehicle was finally collected and rejected under the Consumer Rights Act, the dealership attempted to deduct £610 from my refund, including charges for valeting the faulty vehicle and towing costs.

I ultimately had to issue a Money Claim Online court claim to recover the money owed to me. Even after proceedings had started, there were still attempts to negotiate down what should have been refunded. In the end, the dealership refunded me in full and reimbursed the court fee.

It feels like their style of customer service is to grind the customer down to the point of exhaustion sending ChatGPT messages, hand the customer to different “departments” and haggle. Constant haggling! It felt like they were trying to do a deal with me for my money. You have to hold your ground with this business.

This was, without question, the worst customer service experience I have ever dealt with. Customers should not have to resort to legal proceedings simply to obtain a refund they are legally entitled to for a faulty vehicle.

Thankfully I eventually recovered my money, but only after weeks of stress, arguments, delays, and completely avoidable hassle.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others to think very carefully before purchasing a vehicle from this dealership

I’ve had a pretty frustrating experience with Cuckoo Fibre overall, despite some positives.

To start with the good: when the connection actually works, the speeds are genuinely very good. Streaming, downloads, and general browsing are all fast and stable at times, which is what you’d hope for from a fibre provider.

However, the issues around everything else have really let it down.

Customer service has been a major pain point. It often feels like the support team doesn’t fully understand what’s being asked, even for relatively simple requests. On multiple occasions, I’ve tried to get straightforward changes made and it’s either taken far too long or hasn’t been done correctly at all.

A big limitation is the lack of control over the router. You can’t make basic network changes yourself — things like opening ports, changing the WiFi password, or even renaming your network. This is incredibly restrictive, especially if you have smart home devices, gaming setups, or anything that requires port forwarding or custom configuration. Most providers allow at least some level of user control, so this feels unnecessarily locked down.

I’ve also had ongoing issues with devices struggling to connect reliably. There have been multiple engineer visits, and while they’ve confirmed there is a problem, no one seems able to identify the root cause. To make matters worse, the engineers aren’t directly employed by Cuckoo, so there’s a bit of a disconnect in accountability and follow-up.

On the administrative side, things haven’t been much better. I submitted a subject access request over 2.5 months ago and am still waiting for a response, which is well beyond expected timeframes. Formal complaints also seem to disappear into a void — I’m told responses have been sent, but I’ve never actually received them.

In summary, while the raw internet speeds are strong, the lack of router control, poor customer support, unresolved technical issues, and slow (or nonexistent) responses to formal requests make this a difficult service to recommend.

I’m honestly really disappointed with my experience at Christmas Tree Farm and feel I need to warn other families.

My toddler child was bitten by a pig during our visit. The bite broke the skin and drew blood. I reported this immediately to a member of staff and asked whether I should be concerned about tetanus or infection. The response was completely dismissive—there was no concern, no advice, and no support offered.

I asked to speak to the manager, but the attitude didn’t improve. I was told that “kids get bitten” and that it is down to parents because there are signs in place. However, the signs are in green—not a colour typically associated with danger—and more importantly, a young child cannot read or understand signage. That is not an adequate safety measure in an environment aimed at families.

The pigs are able to get their heads through the fencing, meaning children can easily get too close. There is no mesh, no secondary barrier, and nothing effective in place to prevent contact. When I raised this, I was told that mesh “wouldn’t last,” with no alternative solution offered.

What concerned me most was being told that incidents like this are not routinely recorded. I had to insist that my child’s injury was written in the accident book, and even then, the manager stated he didn’t really consider it an “accident.” This raises serious concerns about how safety is managed.

Following the incident, I had to spend several hours in hospital with my child, who has since been prescribed antibiotics due to the bite. Thankfully, their tetanus vaccinations are up to date, but this does not make the situation acceptable. The injury could have been far more serious, as pigs are capable of causing severe damage.

What was most upsetting was the complete lack of care or empathy shown. At no point did anyone ask if my child was okay or needed medical attention. The situation was handled with no urgency or concern.

I understand that animals can be unpredictable, but that is exactly why proper safety measures must be in place—especially in a setting designed for young children.

In my view, this is a serious safeguarding issue and an accident waiting to happen again. I would strongly urge other families to be extremely cautious when visiting.

The Most Deplorable, Dishonest, Emotionally Draining Scam of a Dealership We’ve Ever Encountered!!!

PCBS isn’t a dealership. It’s a trap. A circus of liars, manipulators and shameless opportunists who will smile in your face while selling you a nightmare on wheels.

We bought a Mercedes S‑Class from these people, and the SAME DAY we collected it, the engine rattled. Why didn’t we hear it before? Because during the test drive the car was in electric‑only mode so the engine never started. A perfectly engineered setup to hide a fault they absolutely knew was there. That’s not an accident that’s deceit dressed up as customer service. We also noticed chipped paintwork which Jaz confirmed he would have rectified.

Within a week, a second fault appeared: a loud whistle on acceleration. Jaz promised both issues would be fixed. Two weeks later we arrived to collect the car… and NOTHING had been touched apart from the diabolical repaint Jaz said was “done”. He even had the audacity to claim the noises “just started” when we arrived. The level of gaslighting was unbelievable.

They told us the car had been sent to Stevensons. We called Stevensons. The car had NEVER been there. They lied without hesitation, without shame, without even blinking. When we saw the car again Jaz had decided to fix the paint work himself by sanding it down and thought that was acceptable.

We paid out of pocket to take the car to a specialist in London, who found a hole in the exhaust and a serious turbo issue  faults that existed long before we ever owned the vehicle.

Then PCBS fabricated statements from Stevensons, claiming they said the turbo wasn’t worth fixing. Another lie. When we asked Adam, the so‑called manager, for proof that the turbo part was on back order with Mercedes, he couldn’t produce a single document. Because nothing was being done. Nothing ever was.

When they finally sent the car to Mercedes Tonbridge, they booked a BASIC HEALTH CHECK instead of a turbo diagnostic. For a car with a KNOWN turbo fault. We had to fix their booking ourselves. Mercedes misdiagnosed it, wasted more time, and eventually admitted it was the turbo all along.

After months of torment PCBS STILL refused to fix the car while having to battle with them to get a courtesy car during this process. We told them repeatedly we wanted it repaired. We even sourced a brand‑new turbo ourselves with a 12‑month warranty. They still dragged their feet. Abs claimed he “couldn’t find a garage” for FOUR MONTHS.

Turbo ordered 8 Oct. Delivered 17 Oct. Car returned 22 Oct. A two‑week repair turned into FIVE MONTHS of stress and lost earnings.

– Terrible refurbished alloys that look like they were done in someone’s shed

We paid for a car we couldn’t use. We lost income. We spent our own money repairing faults we didn’t cause. We lived under constant stress, uncertainty and frustration for FIVE MONTHS because PCBS couldn’t tell the truth if their lives depended on it.

And after everything, every lie, every delay, every fabricated excuse  we asked for a basic three‑month warranty. The bare minimum any decent dealership offers without blinking.

They refused. Their excuse? The case was “too complicated.”

PCBS are charming before the sale and utterly vile after. They sold us a faulty car, hid faults, lied about repairs, fabricated information, ignored us for months, and left us financially and emotionally drained.

After 10 days with no update, I contacted them and was given a delivery date of Wednesday 15th April. The scooter did not arrive. My calls went unanswered.

I eventually spoke to Connor on 16th April and was told there was an issue and I would receive an update that afternoon. I did not. I was then told delivery would be 17th April. Again, nothing arrived.

I later spoke to Dana, who offered an “upgrade” as a goodwill gesture due to the delays and confirmed delivery for 18th April. Once again, no delivery and no communication.

I was repeatedly assured that the replacement scooter had the exact same specifications. This was extremely important due to my access requirements.

A Roadmaster Plus was finally delivered on 20th April. It was immediately clear it was significantly larger. After measuring, it was approximately 3 inches wider and longer than the Galaxy 2. It was impossible to get into my home.

I am a full-time wheelchair user, and the scooter had to be left outside, blocking access to my home and garden. The driver left without resolving the issue.

I reported this straight away and was told I would receive a callback. Connor contacted me on 21st April and agreed to send the correct Galaxy 2.

Collection of the incorrect scooter was promised for 22nd April, but this did not happen. A further collection attempt on 27th April failed due to incorrect details being provided. The scooter was eventually collected on 28th April — over a week after delivery, during which time it blocked access to my property.

I was then told new Galaxy 2 stock had arrived and was promised further updates, but once again, no callbacks were made.

It is now approaching 7 weeks since I originally placed and paid for this order in full, and I remain without the scooter I ordered or my money returned.

I have now escalated this matter to Trading Standards and my bank. I have a full paper trail including emails, call logs, and recordings to support every part of this review.

This experience has been extremely stressful and completely unacceptable. I would strongly advise others to avoid this company. You only have to look at the other 1 star reviews as it appears to be an ongoing trend with this company.

I would also like to make clear that every statement within this review is factual and supported by evidence in my possession.

I was told it was an “updated version” of the same model, however it was a lower specification and not what I had paid for, so I refused delivery.
Following this, I made multiple attempts to resolve the issue by phone and email throughout April. On each occasion I was told I would receive a callback, which did not happen.
I was then informed the original scooter I had ordered was no longer available. Buy British? Don't bother. A predatory and frustrating experience. Rating: 1 / 5

The UK Brand Myth: I paid a significant premium for these locks because I wanted to support a UK business and have the peace of mind of London-based support. It was a massive mistake. Simpled is a corporate facade operating out of a WeWork address, selling fragile hardware with a support system designed to stall and frustrate.

Pricing Chaos: There is zero consistency in their pricing. They list these locks at £169 on their website, sometimes discounted to £99, while charging £139 on Amazon. It is a blatant attempt to see how much they can squeeze out of you.

The Hardware Saga: I ordered three units initially. One arrived with a broken front panel. Despite the heavy price tag, this isn't some bespoke system. The locks run entirely on a basic, third-party app (TTLock). Worse yet, the core biometric feature is practically useless; the fingerprint sensor is so unreliable that the lock mostly wouldn't open even after 8 to 10 attempts. The replacement I eventually received for the broken unit appeared to be a used customer return and was just as defective.

The Most Ridiculous Part: When I had to replace another faulty component, the shipping took a full week. To make matters worse, they had the audacity to blame me for a part that broke while I was simply trying to fix their defective hardware. They then tried to charge me an extra £33 for the replacement part. I was only in that position because their original product was faulty, yet they tried to turn it into a profit-making opportunity.

The Support Nightmare: They boast about UK resident support, yet it routinely took them 24 hours or more to reply to a basic email. I spent a week in an exhausting loop of stalling tactics. Even after management admitted they got many things wrong, they suggested a resolution with an offer I didn't even ask for. Given the days of physical labor and the sheer administrative hassle they caused, the offer was quite frankly insulting anyway!

The Truth: I have since ripped these out and replaced them with alternative locks that cost only £40. To be honest, the £40 replacements are far superior in every way. The biometrics work instantly and the build quality puts Simpled to shame.

The Verdict: Save your money, your time, and your doors. You can buy a better product for £40 elsewhere and avoid the headache of a company that cares more about its image than its customers.

It is up to you to make your own mind up, but I have done the legwork so you don't have to.

UPDATE: The owner has replied below attempting to blame an "inexperienced team member." This is completely false. It was their Customer Service Manager who offered me an insulting token gesture after a week of stalling. Now they are suggesting I should have left a voicemail, despite them taking 24 plus hours to reply to basic emails.

Blaming your staff and even your customers instead of taking responsibility tells you everything you need to know about this company.

Title: £300 a year lost for being a loyal customer

As a long-standing customer with a substantial savings balance, I was very disappointed to discover I am receiving a significantly lower interest rate than what is currently offered to new customers on similar accounts.

This is not a small difference — it equates to hundreds of pounds per year in lost interest.

I raised this as a formal complaint, but the response did not explain why existing customers are left on lower rates or offer any meaningful solution. There is also no clear or proactive way to ensure customers are moved to more competitive rates.

I understand banks offer incentives to attract new customers, but this feels like a clear loyalty penalty. Existing customers should not be disadvantaged in this way.

Very disappointing experience.

I’m disappointed that Monument is offering 4.51% to new savers while existing long-term customers are left on a much lower rate of 3.77%.

That gap feels unfair, especially when you require a minimum balance of £25k, because the savings are substantial and the difference in interest really adds up over time.

I raised this concern and the reply was polite, but it did not properly address why loyal customers are left behind or offer a clear solution.

A bank that wants trust from savers should treat existing customers fairly as well as new ones.

I took my car to Endeavour Automotive (official Volvo servicing) and aside from Ann Marie at reception — who was genuinely lovely — the experience was extremely poor.

I made it very clear from the start that this is a second-hand car that’s new to us, and that I wanted a FULL safety check. I also highlighted that both front tyres had slow leaks and explained we were about to go on a long journey. I specifically asked if tyres could be replaced on-site the same day at Swiss Cottage and was told yes. I was also assured I’d receive a FULL health check report.

When I dropped the car off, I repeated everything in person and provided a clear list: tyres, brake pads, rust, wing mirror light, and air filter.

A few hours later, the report came back with only a few flags. No mention of the rust being checked as part of the check list, or the full list of points I explicitly asked for. So much for a “full check.”

Then I was told they couldn’t replace the tyres, despite previously being told that they could, and was told to go elsewhere.

They didn’t pick up on basic safety issues. I took the car straight to Kwik Fit, where I was told the rear tyres were at just 18 PSI. That is a fundamental safety check that was completely missed. Made worse by the fact that they included the back tyres in the health check and said they were up to scratch.

Even small details were ignored — my windscreen washer fluid was empty and wasn’t topped up or flagged despite showing a notice on the dash screen.

Now, just days later, the car is showing signs of stalling. A proper inspection might have caught this before a long journey, which is exactly why I booked the car in.

There was zero feedback on the rust I asked about in the actual written report, and the customer service on the phone before coming to collect the car was abrupt to the point of being rude—I was effectively cut off mid-question.

What should have been a simple, all-in-one service turned into multiple trips and unnecessary stress on a busy work day.

Overall, this visit felt careless, incomplete, and poorly communicated. For an authorised Volvo service centre, the standard is low. I’ve had more thorough and professional service from basic garages.

We paid for a full-page advert in a local golf club brochure with Ludis Marketing Consulting Ltd, including confirmation we would be the only sports injury clinic featured.

We worked with their designer, had the artwork approved, and paid 50% upfront — so they were fully aware of our advert and involvement.

However, when the brochure was published, our advert was not included at all, and another physiotherapy company appeared instead. We were never informed — we only discovered this ourselves when visiting the club.

We have since been told that another company had taken the slot before us. However, this was not communicated at any stage, despite us proceeding with the booking, working with their designer, and receiving confirmation that the artwork had been approved.

If the slot was unavailable, this should have been clearly communicated before any work was carried out.

For completeness, we have rechecked our correspondence and cannot find any apology or explanation provided at the time.

This had a direct impact on our business, as we had already started building a relationship with the club based on this opportunity and the company that was featured has since gone on to secure an ongoing partnership there.

We were also provided with an email outlining a 5,000 print run and wide distribution, but the terms and conditions only guarantee 1,000 copies at the club, with any further distribution at their discretion. This discrepancy should be made clearer to clients.

A refund was eventually issued, but only after chasing, and this does not account for the time invested working with their designer or the lost marketing opportunity.

We would strongly advise other businesses to proceed with caution and ensure all commitments are clearly documented.

one_star_reviews.text:
I strongly advise against doing business with D&B Militaria if you are an international buyer.

My experience with them was highly negative and highlights serious issues with transparency, communication, and basic business practices.

Initially, after placing the order, they confirmed the total amount (including shipping), which I paid in full, despite the shipping cost already being increased from the originally provided information. After payment, I had to make an inquiry myself to confirm receipt of funds, as no notification was provided even after several days. After receiving the payment, they unilaterally began increasing the costs again — first due to an alleged shipping miscalculation, and only after I requested supporting evidence did they claim the increase was actually also due to “missing” bank transfer fees.

When I requested clarification and supporting evidence (such as a postal receipt or a cost breakdown), they failed to provide it. I did not agree to pay more at this point since the mistake was not on my side. Instead, they referred to their terms and conditions, which do not clearly state the requirements they later tried to enforce (e.g. that the buyer must cover all bank fees or that SHA transfers are not accepted - regarding the missing bank transfer fees). Being cornered with the implicit statement that they can simply cancel the order if I did not comply is unacceptable, especially considering that they had already received my payment and misscalculations were made on their side.
At the end I canceled the order and promptly received the funds, of course minus the bank transfer fees.

Additional concerns:
Unclear and contradictory terms and conditions – interpreted selectively and always to the customer’s disadvantage
Costs changing after payment has been completed, which is unacceptable
Poor communication – responses are vague and lack concrete solutions
Shifting responsibility for their own mistakes onto the customer (incorrect shipping estimates, bank fees)

To conclude:
This is a company with a non-transparent approach to business, where terms are adjusted on the fly and consistently to the detriment of the customer. Such practices are unprofessional and risky, especially for international buyers. It is also worth noting that this was a relatively low-value shortfall of funds, so it is difficult to understand why a company would be willing to compromise its credibility and fair business practices over such a minor amount.

I was also informed—only at that stage—that the practitioner I had booked with does not perform 1ml treatments. This was not disclosed at the time of booking, making the visit unproductive.

I was then asked to return on Friday to potentially see another practitioner. Despite arriving early as advised, I was not seen within my scheduled time and had to leave due to prior commitments. I returned later that day with my children and was finally assessed, at which point I was informed that treatment would not proceed.

Multiple appointments, long wait times, and inconsistent handling of the process resulted in unnecessary inconvenience.

I was very disappointed by the lack of empathy shown by both the staff and owners of Your Best Car
My Lexus car was stolen in March and as I was told it was unlikely to be recovered and,as I have a disabled wife and a vehicle is essential, I went to Your Best Car the next day, as I had seen they had an identical car to mine, the same year and mileage.
I explained my predicament to them and, although they don’t allow test drives, I agreed to buy the car.
Two days later I was informed by the police that they had recovered the car in London. I informed Your Best Car immediately as I had no idea what condition the car was in as I clearly didn’t want to end up with two cars.
I picked up the car from the London Police pound a couple of days later and it was fine. I informed Your Best Car that I did not want to complete the purchase but they refused to refund my £1,000 deposit, despite the fact that they only took it off the market for five days. I even offered to pay for any out of pocket costs like cleaning.
They failed to tell me at the time of the sale that I could have reserved the car for up to seven days and the deposit would have been repayable as is stated in their Terms and Conditions. It would have been helpful if they had told me about this at the time, in view of my circumstances.
During the whole five days I constantly kept Your Best Car informed of the situation.
I wrote a letter setting out the full circumstances of my case but haven’t received the courtesy of a reply
I have always believed in giving business to local companies but, needless to say, this whole episode has left a lasting bad taste and has done nothing to foster customer relations.

**Your Best Car Successfully Sued**

In January 2022, myself and my wife agreed to purchase a Range Rover Sport from Your Best Car. Following the remote negotiations, I agreed to travel five and a half hours from our home in Chester to the Show yard in Cranbrook to collect the car and trade our 15 plate Range Rover in.

When I arrived, the salesman Jack, welcome me and we went to his office to de-register our number plate from our car and was helpful enough to give me access to his laptop to do so.

As all the documents were already completed by my wife before I arrived, I then went to check the car before I drove it home. When walking around I noticed that the tyre tread was low and it was clear that the tracking was out.

I explained to Jack that we would not accept the car in that condition and the tyre potentially ‘could’ be illegal. He refused to replace the tyre or credit me the equivalent value for a new one  and I explained that we were cancelling the deal. He said that our car was not in the condition that was described and would not oblige.

I requested our £500 deposit back and Jack very smuggly, insisted that we would not be getting it back as their ‘terms and conditions’ signed day my wife said that they would charge £495 to cancel the agreement and return the money to the finance company.

I returned home and confirmed with the finance company that there was not penalty to return the finance and emailed Your Best Car once again requesting the refund quoting ‘The Consumer Contracts (Information, cancelation and additional fees) Regulations 2013’ which states that the deposit must be returned otherwise we would move forward with a claim in the county courts.

We received a very bolshy response from Ashley from Your Best Car saying that they would not be returning the money and if we did pursued them to recover the money then they would counter clam for a further £495 plus compensation for their time to prepare the car.

We lodged our claim with the courts and sure enough Your Best Car issued their counter claim.

Following a few delays due to my wife's availability to attend a zoom hearing,  we attended a hearing on 10th July 2023, where we were successful in our claim and we were awarded our deposit back, plus the court and hearing fee.

The judge ruled that the clause in the Your Best Cars contract was unfair and unenforceable and made it very clear to the Managing Director Mr Woolger that it went against the Consumer Contract Regulations Act and threw out his pathetic (My view) counter claim.

It was unfortunate that we had to take Mr Woolger and Your Best Car to the small claims court to recover our rightful hard earned money, but delighted with the outcome.

We are concerned that there are no doubt other customers that have succumbed to this clause in the T’s & C’s and this is reason why we have decided to write this review. We have also contacted trading standards to inform them of the case and outcome.

I have no doubt that Your Best Car have had some very happy customers however Mr Woolger’s own LinkedIn profile states that his ‘goal is to build a reputable, recognised, modern brand within the motor industry centered on providing an 'outstanding customer experience, but from our particular experience, he has certainly failed to deliver this on occasion

We would encourage him and his team to remember his own business ethos in future disputed sales and will consider removing this clause from their contracts immediately so that no other customer is left out of pocket if they decide to cancel the agreement.

Attached is the picture of the tyre in question and the redacted documentation from the court proving our successful claim.

Please be very cautions when buying from this company and please check the T’s & C’s otherwise you may have to battle through the courts to get your money back!

I booked to shop here with my bridal party and mums and the initial engagement was great, had a phone call to discuss style and vision, sent over ideas etc, all the usual process. Upon arriving at the venue there weren’t enough chairs for my group, even tho we’d discussed how many people were coming. It was also a boiling day with temps around 25 degrees and no one was offered water. The floor looked dirty and worn despite being asked to remove shoes. And I was told the gowns are a little “worn” as it’s the “end of season”. They weren’t worn they were just dirty tbh, most had makeup marks and grey ish stains on them.

I got started on a few that I had chosen and a few that were pulled out for me. The dresses themselves were nice, but honestly feel other bridal shops in town have a better selection for you to try (and are also better cared for). I’d given my size in advance, I am generally a solid size 10. Most of the dresses I tried on were too small for me, their sample size in store the I tried on were made for much smaller sized people. The dresses were being held together by hair ties around buttons (see photos) 🥴 which did not give “high end boutique” at all. How was I meant to envisage it with brown hair ties holding it together?? Not professional at all. All other shops I’ve been to had a size up and then they clipped you in so you could see the perfect fit. Thankfully I am very secure in my body, but I can’t imagine what that would do to someone who was more body conscious than me.

I share this experience so others can make an informed decision. about dealing with this retailer. The Law is there to protect everybody, so this matter continues to be challenged, and I will continue to raise awareness of my treatment. I regret to say that my experience with Taylor’s Pitstop has been deeply disappointing, both in terms of service and professionalism.

I initially brought my vehicle here last year to address an oil leak, which, regrettably, appears not to have been properly resolved. Upon returning recently to investigate the ongoing issue, I was advised that additional work was required. Having already obtained a quote elsewhere following my MOT, I agreed to proceed with Taylor’s based on a telephone quotation of £1,444 (including VAT), alongside a promised discount on four new tyres.

I gave clear authorisation for the work to proceed. However, the following day I received an abrupt call from another staff member requesting to revisit details already agreed. When I explained I was unavailable due to an urgent appointment, I was met with a rather dismissive response suggesting the work would not continue. This, I was told, was due to a lack of internal notes — an operational failing that should not fall upon the customer.

Upon collection of my vehicle, I discovered that the agreed tyre discount had not been applied. When I raised this, I was told I was expected simply to pay and collect the car, without discussion. This approach was wholly unacceptable, particularly given that the discount had been a deciding factor in proceeding with the work.

What followed was even more concerning. In the absence of a manager on site, I was eventually directed to two individuals from another department. While one gentleman was courteous and attempted to assist, the other displayed behaviour that I can only describe as inappropriate and deeply uncomfortable. I was asked a series of irrelevant personal questions — including where I live, what I do for a living, and where I am originally from — none of which had any bearing on resolving the issue at hand.

Despite acknowledging the prior agreement, he initially refused to honour the tyre discount, instead offering a “free service” in the future — an offer which felt both dismissive and patronising. Matters deteriorated further when he made an entirely inappropriate and xenophobic comparison, which I found both offensive and unacceptable in a professional setting.

At this point, the issue was no longer about the discount, but about principle, respect, and basic standards of customer care. Only after I expressed my dissatisfaction — and sought advice from a third party — was the originally promised discount reluctantly applied.

For a service costing in excess of £1,400, one would expect competence, clear communication, and above all, respect. Unfortunately, my experience reflected none of these.

I would strongly caution others — particularly women and those who may feel vulnerable in such environments — to consider carefully before using this establishment. Professionalism should not be conditional, nor should customers feel judged or diminished when seeking a service they are paying for.

A thoroughly disappointing experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Prospective buyers should be aware of highly misleading pricing practices when searching for this company online. When searching for the Loake Kensington loafers, this retailer’s organic Google search listing prominently displays a base price of £249.17 with free delivery. over £50 cheaper than direct from manufacture. This gives the immediate impression of being the final consumer cost, allowing them to rank on search engines with an artificially low price compared to honest competitors.

However, once you click through to the website, it becomes clear that this advertised £249.17 price is completely exclusive of VAT, with the actual retail price jumping to £299.00. Simple see the screenshots.

While the ASA does not regulate organic search results, the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs) absolutely applies to online businesses selling to UK consumers. Displaying an ex-VAT price to everyday retail shoppers without immediate, prominent qualification is a misleading omission.

It forces consumers to take a transactional action, clicking through and browsing, based on false pretenses. This systematic lack of transparency is incredibly deceptive and has been reported to Trading Standards via Citizens Advice for formal investigation.

I want to provide a factual account of my experience with Pembroke Management Company and explain why this negative review has been left.

Following advice from my solicitor, I contacted Pembroke to request a management pack after previous emails had gone unanswered. During my initial call, I was informed that an invoice would be issued, but there was no upfront mention of the £330 + VAT (£396 total) fee for providing this document. I asked to speak with someone who might have the authority to expedite the request, such as a manager or supervisor, but this was repeatedly refused. The call was then terminated.

Subsequent attempts to contact them from my phone went unanswered. However, when calling from my partner’s phone, the call was picked up. I explained the situation again, only to receive no assistance, no solutions, and the call was again ended abruptly. This happened twice.

For clarity, while I was understandably frustrated during these interactions, I did not engage in any abusive behaviour—no name-calling or inappropriate language was used. I simply questioned the lack of assistance and competence in handling what should be a routine request.
