one_star_reviews.text:
Save your time, money, patience and mental wellbeing by avoiding this company. They made the original application and renting process extremely easy, but as soon as we signed the contract and handed over the money, the efficiency and care stopped.

Extremely unhelpful staff, poor, frustrating communication loops and a maddening check-out process made it a terrible experience for me and my flatmates. Every time we called to chase up action on an issue, the relevant person always seemed to be just going into a meeting, and it's only when we notified them that worsening issues would cause genuine damage to the property did they intervene.

They tried to take a significant portion of money out of our deposit, which they had no right to do, as can be proven by the enormous paper trail of communication we built during our tenancy. When we challenged it, as was our right, Lexadon relented. Advice to current tenants would be to catalogue everything, stand your ground and don't be afraid to raise disputes with TDS.

Renting in London can be hard enough as it is - Lexadon only make it ten times worse. AVOID!

Great team up to the point of signing documents. Post-signature quite a disappointing service. Upon moving in there were multiple issues with our rental property that were agreed to be remediated before moving in, in addition to more issues once we had the keys including a water leak, broken fittings, etc.

Over email we were passed around and heard little contact. Most of the problems raised are still outstanding despite being told they were getting looked into, and we now struggle to hear a response from the team. Quite disappointing and put a damper on our move.

Our experience with Lexadon Property Group was wholly unacceptable and demonstrated a consistent pattern of negligence and disregard for tenant welfare.

Severe black mould was reported no fewer than 20 times over the course of the year. Rather than addressing the root cause, we were repeatedly told to “wipe it off with a towel,” and their only action was to paint over it. The situation escalated to the point where mould spread onto our clothes and shoes. A review of other tenant feedback indicates this is not an isolated incident, but a recurring issue across multiple properties they manage.

The bottom bedroom flooded on two separate occasions, resulting in the destruction of personal belongings. On both occasions, the issue was met with prolonged inaction and weeks of unresponsiveness, with no meaningful effort to resolve the damage or prevent recurrence.

Hygiene and maintenance standards were equally concerning. Slugs were entering the property through the shower, highlighting serious underlying issues with the condition of the building. Upon moving in, it was evident the property had not been inspected or properly cleaned following the previous tenants. We were forced to demand a basic standard of cleanliness before it was addressed.

Customer service throughout was appalling—dismissive, unresponsive, and entirely lacking in accountability. The cumulative effect of these failures caused significant and ongoing stress and anxiety.

This level of mismanagement is unacceptable. Avoid at all costs.

When we moved in to our flat, we were met with blood stained mattresses and mouldy walls that you would’ve expect to be clean when you move in - this was not the case when renting from Lexadon, and we have been left in the dark by the maintenance team, or expected to pay for replacing faulty equipment ourselves.

I would avoid renting from Lexadon - once they have your money, they don’t care for your wellbeing and give no thought to your health and safety.

MATT finish is IMPOSSIBLE to keep clean

Do NOT buy the MATT finish.

I have found it impossible to keep these doors looking good from the outset.

I think there is something about the physical characteristics of the very finely textured matt finish which means that even the slightest mark reflects the light unevenly from some angles in some lighting conditions, causing the finish to look dirty, stained, smeared and worn, whilst looking ok from other angles and in different lighting - e.g. switching from daylight to artificial light.

This phenomenon is present on a large scale after any attempt to clean the surface in the recommended manner. I have tried very carefully and on several occasions, following their advice to the letter, but still with the same unsatisfactory result.

Following this review, I had further exchanges with this trader. I received the same advice about cleaning, which still did not work.

They said I could send a door back to them (at my expense) so they could send it back to the factory to compare it with the 'foil' they are using (by which I presume the mean the plastic film they bond to the MDF to give the finish).

I couldn't see the point in this because the quality of the new materials isn't in question; out of the box, the doors look very nice indeed. It is their ability to retain their looks with even the slightest exposure to a kitchen environment which is doubtful; in other words, the 'fitness for purpose' of the finish.

I responded to them saying so, and informing them of my intention to replace the doors.

All they need to do is procure a sample of the supermatt marine blue finish of their own product and try some simple tests to simulate exposure to common kitchen stains and then try applying their own cleaning advice. But apparently, this is beyond them.

They responded offering me 25% discount on replacements. I won't be taking them up on this offer for the obvious reason that I cannot be sure this whole customer experience won't be repeated.

I hope this description of my experience with this trader helps others to make informed judgements about this company and their products.

They do have a very good free sample service, so, if you want to test a sample for yourself, you can do so very easily and for free.

We travelled with Mercury Holidays on the Vietnam and Cambodia Odyssey (Winter) tour from 27 November 2025 for 16 days.
Pros:
The people of Vietnam and Cambodia were warm and welcoming, and the destinations visited were beautiful, informative, and culturally enriching.
Cons:
The Halong Bay cruise on the Victory Star was extremely disappointing. The boat appeared old and poorly maintained, with our cabin showing significant wear, exposed plumbing, and a generally rundown condition that fell well below expectations. Embarkation and disembarkation on both the Halong Bay and Mekong cruises also raised safety concerns, with narrow, unstable planks used for access. Some passengers felt unsafe and refused to disembark.

The use of overnight train travel was also problematic. Platform heights did not align with the carriages, making boarding difficult, particularly with large suitcases. Narrow corridors, uneven platforms, and the need to cross railway tracks with heavy luggage created unsafe conditions, resulting in one passenger falling and being injured.

Food throughout the tour was consistently poor. Meals were repetitive and of low quality, often shared in an unhygienic manner. Desserts were minimal, mainly very small cuts of fruits, and drinks were charged at prices significantly higher than local restaurants.

Overall, while the destinations and local people were excellent, several aspects of the tour did not meet the standard expected of a guided holiday.

I have been a member of David Lloyd Brighton Marina for five months. I do not usually write reviews, but as the club is closed today due to there being “no water at the club”, I am using the gym time I had planned to reflect on my experience, how the club is managed, and whether it represents value for money.

The positives: the front desk staff are friendly and helpful, and the three introductory personal training sessions included with my membership were genuinely useful and a great way to ease back into the gym (thank you, Josh). The club is also generally cleaned to a decent standard for a very busy club.

Unfortunately, the overall experience is let down by some fundamental and ongoing issues.

David Lloyd Brighton Marina is located right on the seafront although you wouldn't know if by looking out of the windows as they are filthy. I'm not sure they have been cleaned in the five months I have been there. The building itself is old and visibly deteriorating. From the worn exterior and frequently broken front door access, to gym equipment regularly out of order and taped up, the site feels tired and under-maintained.

When I signed up to a 12-month membership, I was assured that the club would be undergoing a major refurbishment within my first year. While this may still be planned, there is currently no visible sign of this happening, nor has there been any communication to members about timelines. At present, several machines are taped up as out of order, which often leaves too few working options for the number of members using the gym at busy times.

There has also been an ongoing issue with hot water since I joined. I don't know if this pre-dates my membership, but there has been no clear explanation of the cause, nor any reassurance that it is being resolved long-term.

I’ve not yet made use of the pool, steam room or sauna due being too busy and over-crowded, which is outside the club’s control, but it is worth noting if those facilities are a key reason for joining.

What has most negatively affected my view of David Lloyd, however, was the increase in my membership fee just two months into a 12-month contract. David Lloyd positions itself as a premium gym and is already the most expensive option in Brighton. While the increase itself was not huge, I did not expect a price rise so soon after signing on an agreed fee. From a consumer perspective, it feels questionable at best.

I will continue to use the club when it reopens and see out the remainder of my membership. However, I will not be renewing and will instead be joining Soho House, which represents far better value for money.

Terrible!

Diabolical.
I’ve had one or two poor customer service experiences in my life, but my weeks-long struggle with Vodafone has left me so demoralised that today after speaking with them for the umpteenth time I announced to my family I was going to bed.
I hold Lasting Power of Attorney for an elderly man aged 98. He had no need for most of the services he had on contract with them, so I cancelled them, with great difficulty. Vodafone made me raise three or four complaints to achieve this, and forced me to handle them each separately. When that side of things finally appeared to be resolved, I requested a pay-as-you-go service for my friend, carefully explaining before proceeding that I would be operating the account. I provided all of my LPA documents, my email and mobile number, and awaited details of the new service that they promised to send via email.
Nothing.
Then commenced another almighty struggle to convince them to allow me to operate the new service, which in law, I am entitled to do. Even after patiently explaining the situation all over again and drawing their attention to the legal documents provided, they would not allow me to access nor operate the new service.
I have had no problems administering my friend’s bank account, commissioning his care from the council, placing his property on the market, etc., as his Lasting Power of Attorney.
The only organisation that simply will not support this elderly gentleman appropriately is Vodafone.
This nightmare odyssey is absolutely worthy of a complaint to Ofcom, if I can stomach it. At this point I genuinely believe I am suffering from C-PTSD as a result of the treatment I have been subjected to by Vodafone, who have passed the buck, stonewalled, lied and gaslit me over the course of multiple calls and emails totalling eight to ten hours over the course of the past four to six weeks.
Avoid Vodafone at all costs.

Review of Vodafone UK

I have just spent over an hour trying to complete a basic account function—changing my eSIM—and it has been an exercise in complete systemic failure.

The chatbot “TOBi” does not provide support; it actively blocks access to it

Calling 191 leads to long, irrelevant menu loops with no meaningful outcome

The system promises an SMS, then disconnects without resolving anything

On repeat attempts, voice input is ignored, keypad-only is forced, and calls are terminated

Critically, the online contact/complaints page is not even functional, removing yet another route to support

At this point, there is no effective way to contact Vodafone to manage my account.

This raises serious legal concerns.

Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, services must be delivered with reasonable care and skill. A telecom provider that makes it impossible for customers to access support—particularly for essential account functions—is arguably failing to meet that obligation.

Further, Ofcom requires telecom providers to maintain accessible and effective complaint handling procedures. A system that traps customers in automated loops, disconnects calls, and provides no working contact channels cannot reasonably be described as accessible or effective.

This is not poor service—it is structural avoidance of customer contact.

If customers cannot communicate with their provider, then the service itself is fundamentally compromised. At that point, the question becomes unavoidable: is this a breach of contract?

Customers should seriously consider whether they are receiving the service they are paying for. If enough people begin cancelling contracts on the basis that support is inaccessible, perhaps standards will improve.

As it stands, this experience is unacceptable and falls far below what should be expected from a major UK telecommunications provider.

one_star_reviews.text:
As a live sound professional working in the music industry for over 10 years and with 2 parents who are professional musicians I have some experience with music shops and techs ranging from small independents to large arena productions.

Unfortunately I have to say that this was the worst and most unprofessional service I have seen in my life.

I'll preface that I'm not a guitar tech and I like to give others work. I therefore trust my instruments to specialists in that field (unfortunately my usual contact was not available for this). Took my custom strat in for an upgrade to pickups and bridge as well as a string change. The job was completely rushed, they drilled extra holes in the guitar to fit the bridge (an upgrade for tone reasons) without making it clear that it would not be in the same position as the original, or even in a compatible position where the guitar could play anything like how it was when i brought it to them.

Although I paid for string change and setup, the guitar came back in an unplayable state, strings were not even stretched in and the intonation was completely off. On the low string you couldn't play above the 11th position without the string being completely dead and entirely out of tune.

When asked why the strings weren't even stretched in (therefore the setup wasn't complete) the reply was that they never stretch in strings! So despite us agreeing that the cost would include setup they didn't even do the most basic of checks to see if the instrument was playable (it wasn't).

I therefore tried to dial the settings in myself, was unable to after 4 hours trying and returned the guitar to them to undo the mod to revert back to the previous bridge. This cost me the ability to use the whammy which I can live with but they also charged me extra to put right the original rushed hack job. When I got home (deciding to install strings myself this time) I found that the screws in the back of the bridge were NOT EVEN FULLY SCREWED IN! Luckily I noticed this or it could have ruined the instrument forever had I put any more pressure on the loose bridge since the structural integrity has been weakened by the original bridge mod re-dowel. I therefore completed that myself and thankfully have the guitar at least playable.

I expect experts to advise and protect me in this kind of situation before drilling holes, not just blindly do my upgrade regardless of the outcome then advise me it's going to cost more when there is potential risk of damage. At no point did they allude to any potential risk or even give me the option to back out after it wasn't as expected, they just went ahead and told me it would cost more.

Can't recall ever having to write this kind of negative review before... AVOID this shop for any kind of repair work and don't assume they even know how to set up a guitar they might sell you properly. Wish I had just gone to Youtube videos and saved the £75 (+ hardware) and damage to my guitar as opposed to trusting this shop but other reviews seemed OK and I was hoping I might have a good experience and make contacts for future work. I would have aborted the bridge and just done the pickups if it was left in my hands. I feel any responsible tech would have given an option in that respect before they started making holes.

There is also some ground buzz at occasional times now which wasn't there before, I have yet to troubleshoot this fully but suspect I will also have to double-check the work done on the pickup install.

The entire experience was extremely depressing on top of an already terrible year for me (perhaps I'm cursed or perhaps they judged a book by it's cover and thought they could rip me off). Maybe if others have had a good experience they put a different tech on the job but I would be remiss if I didn't warn against trusting Badlands to perform any repair or maintenance work.

Sorry guys but this is a very fair review. I gave it half a week to cool off before writing and I'm also somewhat relieved that my guitar is not totally destroyed.

I used Skyscanner to find and compare flight options and was directed to GoToGate for a booking. Unfortunately, my experience that followed was extremely disappointing.

During the final payment stage, the advertised fare repeatedly increased on multiple occasions, following the same pattern each time. Temporary PayPal authorizations were also generated, creating inconvenience and temporarily affecting my available card limit.

Despite repeated reports and escalations, no clear solution or timeframe was provided. Most surprisingly, I was eventually advised to book directly with the airline instead.

My main disappointment is not only with the booking provider itself, but also with the fact that I trusted Skyscanner to recommend reliable partners. As a customer, I reasonably expect platforms to carefully assess the quality, transparency, and reliability of the companies they promote.

This experience disrupted travel plans already organized with friends and created unnecessary stress and logistical difficulties. I hope Skyscanner reviews the standards applied when recommending booking partners in order to better protect customers.
Cant speak to no one

★☆☆☆☆

I’ve been traveling the world for over 15 years, across more than 40 countries—often revisiting the same destinations 3 to 5 times. Throughout all those years, Skyscanner was always my first stop when booking flights. It was a tool I trusted. That’s exactly why this review is so disappointing to write.

Over the past few years, the platform has become increasingly unreliable. Misleading pricing has become the norm rather than the exception. You’re drawn in by an attractive fare, only to be redirected through layers of third-party sites, forced to enter all your personal details—right until the final step—where suddenly the price changes, or you’re asked to call an agent to proceed. It feels less like booking a flight and more like being led into a trap. What’s worse is that Skyscanner seems fully aware of this pattern, yet does nothing to meaningfully address it.

But the real issue—the one that turns frustration into distrust—is their car rental service.

I’ve often used competitors like Rentalcars.com, and while Skyscanner sometimes appears slightly cheaper for the same dates, that “cheaper” option comes at a cost. Many of the rental companies listed with high ratings (8+ or even 9+) simply do not match reality. A quick check on Google reveals shockingly low ratings—often below 2—and unfortunately, those ratings reflect the truth.

During our recent Easter trip to Italy, I booked a Mini Cooper Clubman automatic through a provider on Skyscanner with a rating in the 9s. What we actually experienced felt like something out of a cautionary tale.

When I arrived, there were just two customers ahead of me—but the staff member processed each one at an excruciating pace, taking 45 minutes per person, typing with two fingers, completely unhurried. I waited 1 hour and 30 minutes just to reach the counter.

Then came the real problem.

The car I had reserved didn’t exist.

Instead, I was offered a completely different vehicle—a manual Ford Focus—unsuitable for my planned drive through the Alps, where an automatic was essential. I insisted, and after some reluctant phone calls, they managed to find an automatic car. But even that solution collapsed: the smart key didn’t work. Another 40 minutes passed.

At that point, the employee—clearly frustrated—complained that his shift had already ended and even threatened to leave, as if the situation were somehow my fault. Behind me, three more customers were waiting, likely heading into the same chaos.

Traveling with two children and facing a 3.5-hour drive ahead, I had no choice left. After a total of 2 hours and 45 minutes of waiting, I accepted the manual Ford Focus I never wanted in the first place.

And through all of this, Skyscanner offered absolutely no support.

No accountability. No verification. No protection for the customer.

A platform that once symbolized convenience and trust has become something else entirely—an unreliable посредник that shifts responsibility while continuing to profit from it.

I can no longer recommend Skyscanner. Not for flights, and certainly not for car rentals.
